gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the makers rate these battery speakers for 45 °C (113 °F) at most, while UC San Diego and Arizona State measured an average of 116 °F of cabin air and 157 °F on the dashboard after one hour parked in the sun, so a speaker kept in the car is above its rated limit on a summer day.
standout_why: I compared carcody.com, itechguides.com and the Avantree Roadtrip page (that page returned HTTP 429, so I couldn't read it). carcody.com already gives the advice: 'Remove portable lithium-battery devices from parked vehicles, particularly in direct sun or hot climates.' It also says the Bose Flex must be 'removed from the vehicle in extreme heat.' itechguides.com only says heat 'can reduce actual runtime.' Neither page gives a maker's temperature limit or a measured cabin temperature, and neither says that visor speakerphones carry the same battery limit. The rival pages already cover auto-wake and auto-reconnect, so those add nothing new.
decides: It doesn't change which speaker to pick. It changes how the shopper has to use one. Every candidate has a lithium battery, the visor speakerphones (Jabra) included, and the maker's ceiling is 45 °C. The plan 'leave it clipped in the car' breaks the rated limit on hot days, whatever the type. So the page should tell the shopper to take the speaker out (or at least out of the sun), and not to charge it from the 12 V socket while the car is hot. Jabra says a hot battery 'may not work temporarily.' A visor unit's auto-wake gives no advantage if the shopper has to take it out anyway. That makes small portable picks like the StormBox Micro 3 and Clip 5 easier to justify than a visor clip.

findings.label: Maximum operating temperature
findings.source_title: JBL Clip 5 – JBL Singapore online store
findings.note: The page says verbatim: 'Maximum operation temperature: 45°C'. This is JBL's own store, but the Singapore one. jbl.com US and support.jbl.com both returned 403, and the English spec-sheet PDF wouldn't parse. The same page lists the battery as 'Li-ion polymer 5.32Wh (equivalent to 3.8 V/1400 mAh)' and the profiles as 'A2DP 1.4, AVRCP 1.6', with no HFP, so the Clip 5 can't take calls.

findings.label: Jabra's battery temperature rule for speakers, and its hot-car warning
findings.value: Keep the battery between 0 °C and 45 °C (32–113 °F); leaving it in a closed car in summer or winter 'will reduce the capacity and lifetime of the battery'
findings.note: This is from the 'Wireless and corded speakers' section. The page also says 'A product with a hot or cold battery may not work temporarily, even when the battery is fully charged' and 'Avoid charging your speaker in extremely high or low temperatures.' It's Jabra's general rule for its speakers, not a Drive-specific spec.

findings.label: Parked-car cabin air temperature after 1 h in sun (average)
findings.source_title: Research Highlight: Hot Cars Can Hit Life-Threatening Levels in Approximately One Hour – Scripps/UC San Diego
findings.note: UC San Diego and Arizona State tested six cars in Tempe, AZ on three summer days. The study was published in the journal Temperature on 2018-05-24. Conversion: (116−32)×5/9 = 46.7 °C, which is 1.7 °C above JBL's 45 °C maximum.

findings.label: Parked-car dashboard surface after 1 h in sun (average)
findings.source_title: Research Highlight: Hot Cars Can Hit Life-Threatening Levels in Approximately One Hour – Scripps/UC San Diego
findings.note: Same study. Seats averaged 123 °F (50.6 °C) and steering wheels 127 °F (52.8 °C). The article's intro also says dashboards 'exceed 165° F', but 157 °F is the study's average. A speaker left on the dash is about 24 °C over a 45 °C rating.

findings.label: Parked-car temperatures after 1 h in shade (average)
findings.source_title: Research Highlight: Hot Cars Can Hit Life-Threatening Levels in Approximately One Hour – Scripps/UC San Diego
findings.note: Even in shade, the dashboard (47.8 °C) is above 45 °C. Cabin air in shade stays under the limit, so for a car parked in shade, 'put it in the door pocket or under the seat' is a reasonable instruction.
